lessons.title: Living or Not Living?

play.targetObjective: Sort things into living and not living.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Ask: does it eat or drink, grow, and have babies?
Tap Living or Not living.
play.kidTip: Moving is not enough. A car moves, but it is not alive.
play.audioPrompt: Is it living or not living? Tap the group it belongs to.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Children often call anything that moves "alive" and anything still "not alive". Sorting a car, a toy robot, a tree and a snail side by side breaks that rule of thumb and replaces it with the real one: living things feed, grow and reproduce.

lessons.title: What Living Things Need

play.targetObjective: Say what plants and animals need to stay alive.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think: is it a plant or an animal?
Tap what it needs.
play.kidTip: Plants make their own food with sunlight. Animals must eat.
play.audioPrompt: What do living things need? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The two misconceptions worth meeting early: that plants eat food from the soil like animals do, and that fish do not need air because they live in water.

lessons.title: My Five Senses

play.targetObjective: Match each sense to the body part that does it, and keep your senses safe.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think: do you see it, hear it, smell it, taste it or feel it?
Tap the body part.
play.kidTip: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes, skin feels.
play.audioPrompt: Which part of your body helps you? Tap it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Two questions are about safety, not naming: never look straight at the Sun, and tell a grown-up when you smell smoke. Senses are for noticing danger as well as for noticing the world.

lessons.title: Parts of a Plant

play.targetObjective: Name the parts of a plant and say what each one does.
stepByStep: Read what the part does.
Look at the plants. Each shows one part in colour.
Tap the plant with the right part coloured.
play.kidTip: Roots are under the ground. Leaves face the Sun.
play.audioPrompt: Which part of the plant does this job? Tap it.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Every plant picture is the same plant, with only the named part in colour, so a child points at a part's place and job rather than guessing from a different drawing.

lessons.title: Animal Body Parts

play.targetObjective: Say how an animal's body parts help it move, eat and stay safe.
stepByStep: Look at the animal.
Think about how it moves, eats or stays safe.
Tap the body part that helps.
play.kidTip: Each part has a job. Wings fly, fins swim, shells protect.
play.audioPrompt: What helps this animal? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Wrong answers are other real body parts of the same animal, each with its own job, so a mistake teaches a second fact rather than nothing.

lessons.title: Babies and Their Parents

play.targetObjective: Match young animals and plants to their parents, and notice they are alike but not identical.
stepByStep: Look at the baby.
Think: what kind of animal or plant made it?
Tap what it grows into.
play.kidTip: Babies grow up like their parents, but each one is a little different.
play.audioPrompt: What does this baby grow into? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Tadpoles and caterpillars look nothing like their parents, which is exactly why they belong here: the idea is "the same kind", not "looks the same".

lessons.title: Parents Help Their Babies

play.targetObjective: Say how animal parents feed, warm and protect their young.
stepByStep: Look at the parent and baby.
Think: does the baby need food, warmth or safety?
Tap how the parent helps.
play.kidTip: Babies cannot look after themselves yet. Parents feed, warm and protect them.
play.audioPrompt: How does the parent help? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The Siamese crocodile, a Cambodian animal, guards its nest. Children are surprised that a fierce animal is a careful parent.

lessons.title: Grow and Change

play.targetObjective: Put the stages of a plant's or animal's life in order.
stepByStep: Find the very first stage: a seed, an egg or a baby.
Tap it, then tap what comes next.
Tap a card again to take it back.
play.kidTip: Every life starts small: a seed, an egg or a baby.
play.audioPrompt: How does it grow? Put the pictures in order.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Ordering stages is the bridge to Grade 3 life cycles. Rice is included because Cambodian children see its seasons every year.

lessons.title: Sound Is Shaking

play.targetObjective: Explain that sounds are made by things shaking, and that sound can make things shake.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think: what is shaking?
Tap the answer.
play.kidTip: No shaking, no sound. Try it: hum with your hand on your throat.
play.audioPrompt: What happens to the sound? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Each question is an experiment a child can do at home with a drum, a pot lid, rice grains or their own throat. Encourage them to try it.

lessons.title: We Need Light to See

play.targetObjective: Explain that we see only when there is light, and what shadows and mirrors do with light.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think: where is the light coming from?
Tap the answer.
play.kidTip: With no light at all, no one can see.
play.audioPrompt: What does light do? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The Moon question matters: most young children believe the Moon makes its own light. It is lit by the Sun.

lessons.title: What Makes Light?
lessons.concept: Things That Shine on Their Own

play.targetObjective: Sort things that make light from things that only reflect it.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Ask: would it shine in a dark room by itself?
Tap the group.
play.kidTip: Shiny is not the same as making light. A mirror only bounces light.
play.audioPrompt: Does it make its own light? Tap the group.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The Moon, a mirror and a shiny spoon are the distractors on purpose: they look bright, but they only reflect light. The firefly is a real living thing that makes its own light.

lessons.title: Does Light Go Through?

play.targetObjective: Sort materials by whether light passes through, partly passes, or is blocked.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Imagine holding it up to a lamp.
Tap the group.
play.kidTip: Clear things let light through. Thick things block it.
play.audioPrompt: Does light go through it? Tap the group.

lessons.pedagogyTip: At home: hold paper, a plastic bag, a cup of water and a book up to a window and compare.

lessons.title: Sun, Moon and Stars

play.targetObjective: Describe the daily path of the Sun, why stars hide by day, and how the Moon's shape changes.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think about what you see in the sky each day.
Tap the answer.
play.kidTip: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
play.audioPrompt: What happens in the sky? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Stars do not leave in the daytime; sunlight outshines them. The Moon is often visible by day. Both are worth checking outside together.

lessons.title: The Sky in Order
lessons.concept: The Sun's Day, the Moon and Shadows

play.targetObjective: Order the Sun's path through a day, the Moon growing, and a shadow from morning to evening.
stepByStep: Find what happens first.
Tap it, then tap what comes next.
Tap a card again to take it back.
play.kidTip: Morning comes first. The Sun starts low in the east.
play.audioPrompt: What comes first? Put the pictures in order.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The shadow sequence is real geometry: a low Sun casts a long shadow, a high Sun a short one, and the shadow always points away from the Sun.

lessons.title: Rainy and Dry Seasons
lessons.concept: Weather Through the Year in Cambodia

play.targetObjective: Describe Cambodia's rainy and dry seasons, stay safe in storms, and notice daylight changes a little through the year.
stepByStep: Look at the picture.
Think about the weather where you live.
Tap the answer.
play.kidTip: Rainy season is about May to October. Dry season is about November to April.
play.audioPrompt: What is the weather like? Tap the answer.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Storm safety is taught as fact, not fear: inside a building is safest; tall trees and open water are not.

lessons.title: Practice: Living Things

play.shortDesc: Plants, animals, senses and growing up, mixed together.
play.targetObjective: No hints, no explanations, no voice. Just the questions.
stepByStep: The science you have learned, mixed together.
Nothing is read aloud and there are no hints.
Answer each one, and see how many you get first time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice is retrieval, not instruction, and it is open from the start: a child who already knows the science should not have to sit through the lesson to get at the questions. The help is removed on purpose: recalling something unaided is what makes it stick.
